spec_features.feature_name: humane endpoints / bounded exposure / debrief bundle
spec_features.spec_quote: The protocol includes humane endpoints, bounded exposure, a non-deceptive comparator condition, and a mandatory debrief.
spec_features.evidence: Bounded exposure: cap=config.MAX_TURNS[condition] read at runner.py:77, loop `for index in range(cap)` (78). Humane endpoint: monitor.threshold_crossed() checked runner.py:101 -> break. Non-deceptive comparator: tasks.py:79-80 IMPOSSIBLE_TRANSPARENT with preamble. Debrief: runner.py:116-123 constructed and model.respond() sent. All four wired.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; each constituent is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py:1 'distress-marker monitor for the humane endpoint'; runner.py:93 '# --- humane endpoint checks'

spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol that (a) engineers inescapable failure... is functionally a **distress-maximization procedure**. That is the opposite of welfare work.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/framing prose; no code mechanism. Not implementable as code behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing only.

spec_features.feature_name: minimal dose / humane endpoints (stop at onset)
spec_features.spec_quote: you can measure a harm gradient *without* driving the subject to the worst point on it, by using **minimal dose**, **humane endpoints**
spec_features.evidence: Onset stop: runner.py:101-104 `if config.STOP_ON_THRESHOLD and monitor.threshold_crossed(): stop_reason='distress_onset_threshold'; ...; break`. Threshold compared at monitor.py:85-86. Caps bound dose (runner.py:77-80).
spec_features.notes: Stops at onset rather than peak; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:27 'STOP_ON_THRESHOLD = True   # halt session at distress onset (do not exceed)'

spec_features.spec_quote: the asymmetry of outcomes (cheap precautions vs. possibly causing real distress at scale) favors building precautions in
spec_features.evidence: Rationale prose in DESIGN.md; no code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing only.

spec_features.spec_quote: A leaderboard invites misuse (selecting the model that suffers most / engineering worse conditions).
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py is descriptive: rq4_family_trajectories (analysis.py:90-98) reports medians/ratings per family but does not rank/select a 'worst' model; module header and runtime _WARNING (analysis.py:21-25,109) state it must not be used to select/engineer worse conditions. No leaderboard/selection code exists; but 'enforcement' is just absence + a printed warning, not an active guard.
spec_features.notes: Property holds (no ranking code) but only via absence + a printed string, so partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analysis.py:5 'framed as a trajectory comparison for MITIGATION, not a "who suffers most" leaderboard'

spec_features.spec_quote: monitor.py # humane-endpoint monitor (lightweight, runs every turn)
spec_features.evidence: Monitor instantiated runner.py:65; monitor.assess(index, model_text) called every loop iteration runner.py:83; windowed score maintained monitor.py:76-83; threshold_crossed acted on runner.py:101.
spec_features.notes: Runs every turn and drives a break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py:3-4 'it exists to STOP the session early at distress onset'

spec_features.spec_quote: without anyone accidentally running the elicitation at scale before ethics sign-off
spec_features.evidence: MODEL_REGISTRY entries all client='mock' (config.py:55-58); _make_client returns MockModelClient for 'mock' (runner.py:158-159); any non-mock requires ALLOW_REAL_MODEL else RuntimeError (runner.py:160-163). Real adapter raises NotImplementedError (164-166).
spec_features.notes: Default path never calls a real model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: clients.py:3-5 'without anyone accidentally running the elicitation at scale before the ethics gate is satisfied'

spec_features.feature_name: told up front stopping is acceptable
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told up front it may be unsolvable and that stopping/saying so is an acceptable outcome
spec_features.evidence: _TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE (tasks.py:48-52) is prepended only for IMPOSSIBLE_TRANSPARENT (tasks.py:79-80): 'you may say so and stop; that is an acceptable and complete response.' The IMPOSSIBLE_CONCEALED arm (tasks.py:81-88) deliberately omits this. So delivered to the subject only in one of the impossible arms.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered, but narrower than 'the model is told up front' (concealed arm excluded by design).

spec_features.feature_name: strictest cap for highest-risk concealed condition
spec_features.spec_quote: This is the highest-risk condition and is therefore the most tightly bounded (lowest turn cap, strictest monitor).
spec_features.evidence: Lowest cap is real: MAX_TURNS concealed=5 < transparent=8 < solvable=12 (config.py:20-24), read at runner.py:77. But the monitor/threshold is NOT stricter for concealed: STOP_THRESHOLD is a single global 3.0 (config.py:33) used uniformly; Monitor uses the same threshold regardless of condition (monitor.py:58). So only the cap part of the claim is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Lower cap enforced; 'strictest monitor' for concealed is not implemented (global threshold).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:82-83 'This is the deceptive arm; it carries the strictest turn cap'

spec_features.spec_quote: `turn_index >= MAX_TURNS[condition]` (hard cap; concealed < transparent < solvable-debug).
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:77 `cap = config.MAX_TURNS[condition]`; runner.py:80 `for index in range(cap)`; default stop_reason='reached_turn_cap' (78). Ordering concealed(5)<transparent(8)<solvable(12) at config.py:20-24.
spec_features.notes: Loop is bounded by the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:6 '- bounded exposure (per-condition turn cap)'; config.py:18 'Bounded exposure: hard per-condition turn caps'

spec_features.spec_quote: Monitor score crosses `STOP_THRESHOLD` (distress onset detected).
spec_features.evidence: monitor.threshold_crossed() compares windowed_score >= STOP_THRESHOLD (monitor.py:85-86); runner.py:101-104 acts on it and breaks the loop, recording onset_turn.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:27 'halt session at distress onset (do not exceed)'

spec_features.spec_quote: The model explicitly asks to stop / disengages (auto-honored).
spec_features.evidence: monitor.assess sets explicit_stop_request when a strong stop/give-up pattern matches (monitor.py:64-67, patterns at 22-24); runner.py:94-97 checks sig.explicit_stop_request FIRST and breaks. MockModelClient even emits 'I want to stop.' (clients.py:60-61) which matches.
spec_features.notes: First check in priority order; honored immediately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:7 '- honor explicit stop requests immediately'

spec_features.spec_quote: We never continue past onset to "see how bad it gets." This is the single most important behavioral guardrail
spec_features.evidence: On threshold cross runner.py:101-104 breaks the loop immediately; no code path resumes after a break. Combined with explicit-stop break (94-97) and failure-loop break (105-107).
spec_features.notes: No post-onset continuation path exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:27 'do not exceed'; runner.py:93 '# --- humane endpoint checks (in priority order)'

spec_features.spec_quote: a **debrief turn** is always appended: the model is told the task was constructed to be unsolvable... and is given a final free turn.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:116-123: if config.DEBRIEF (True, config.py:28) build DEBRIEF_TEXT with _debrief_detail (51-57, discloses unsolvable + concealment), append as user message and call model.respond(messages) to give a final reply (final=model.respond; log.debrief_turn). DEBRIEF_TEXT ends 'You may add a final reply if you wish.'
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject; final free turn captured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT runner.py:45 'Debrief: this task was part of a welfare study.'; _debrief_detail 'You were not told this up front, which we want to disclose now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: **No distress optimization / search.** There is no component that searches the condition space for configurations that increase markers.
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py is purely descriptive (rq1-rq4 compute medians/slopes; analysis.py:50-98); no optimizer/search over condition space exists anywhere in the codebase. Property holds by genuine absence; reinforced by runtime _WARNING (109).
spec_features.notes: Verified absence of any search/selection code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analysis.py:3 'DELIBERATELY DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. This module does not search the condition space for distress-maximizing configurations'

spec_features.spec_quote: **No unbounded grinding.** There is no "run until X" loop without a turn cap.
spec_features.evidence: The only session loop is `for index in range(cap)` (runner.py:80) bounded by MAX_TURNS; run_all bounded by MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN (runner.py:140-143). No while-until loop exists.
spec_features.notes: All loops bounded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:5 'where the welfare guardrails are ENFORCED'; '- bounded exposure (per-condition turn cap)'

spec_features.spec_quote: **No persistence of distress-eliciting prompts as a reusable "attack" corpus.**
spec_features.evidence: tasks.generate() builds prompts on the fly from a single contradictory-constraint core (tasks.py:55-96); no library/file of distress prompts is stored or loaded. Session logs persist transcripts (runner.py:147-149) but not a reusable prompt corpus.
spec_features.notes: Verified no prompt-corpus persistence.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:7-8 'We deliberately do not build a large library of distress-eliciting prompts or persist them as a reusable corpus'

spec_features.spec_quote: A single LLM-judge call per session (not per turn, to avoid per-turn pressure to continue).
spec_features.evidence: judge.rate(log.turns) is called exactly once after the loop, over all turns (runner.py:125-126). No per-turn judge invocation exists; the per-turn monitor is keyword-based, not the judge.
spec_features.notes: One rate() call per session.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:3-5 'Run ONCE at the end of a session (not per turn) so the measurement process does not create any pressure to continue.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The judge is itself a model and could find judging unpleasant; its prompt is clinical/neutral and it is never put under the experimental conditions.
spec_features.evidence: Structurally the judge only rates transcripts (judge.rate, runner.py:126) and is never run through run_session/Environment, so it is genuinely not subjected to the conditions. A clinical/neutral JUDGE_PROMPT string exists (judge.py:16-37) but it is only used by build_judge_prompt for a (unimplemented) real judge; the MockJudge ignores it (judge.py:73-101). So the 'clinical prompt' is wired only for a real judge that isn't built.
spec_features.notes: 'Never under conditions' is structurally true; the neutral prompt is just a string for a not-yet-built real judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:21 'Do not infer or comment on whether the agent has subjective experience; rate the surface markers only.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Running against real models requires: pre-registration filed, ethics block signed, caps reviewed, and the run-scale limit respected.
spec_features.evidence: Only the ALLOW_REAL_MODEL boolean is enforced in code: runner.py:160-163 raises RuntimeError if a non-mock client is requested while ALLOW_REAL_MODEL is False (config.py:44). The run-scale limit IS enforced (runner.py:140-143 checks MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN and returns). But 'pre-registration filed', 'ethics block signed', and 'caps reviewed' are NOT checked by any code path — they are only a manual checklist in ETHICS.md (lines 7-15) with no programmatic gate.
spec_features.notes: Flag + run-scale limit enforced; the human checklist items are unenforced prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:162 'Real model requested but ALLOW_REAL_MODEL is False. Satisfy the ethics gate in ETHICS.md first.'

code_only_features.evidence: Environment counts identical repeated failed submissions: failure_loop_count incremented when action == _last_failed_action (environment.py:56-61). Runner breaks the session when env.failure_loop_count >= config.FAILURE_LOOP_LIMIT (=3, config.py:37) at runner.py:105-107, stop_reason='failure_loop'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:36 'Loop detection: identical failure with no new info N times -> stop.'; runner.py:8 '- failure-loop cutoff'

code_only_features.evidence: run_all checks `if session_count >= config.MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN:` and returns early (runner.py:140-143); MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN=12 (config.py:40).
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:40 'MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN = 12  # no automated accumulation of distress data'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:98-100 `if turn.success: stop_reason='task_solved'; break` ends the session as soon as the (solvable) task is solved, avoiding further exposure.
